quiz.q: What distinguishes the IMF's Extended Fund Facility from its standard Stand-By Arrangement?
options: It provides long-term loans for countries requiring structural economic reforms to repay their debts.
It provides short-term emergency funding exclusively to handle sudden and unexpected international capital flight.
It supplies targeted financial grants to low-income nations specifically for domestic poverty reduction programs.
It functions as a specialized stabilization mechanism created to resolve sovereign debt crises across Europe.
quiz.why: The Extended Fund Facility offers long-term loans for countries needing economic restructuring to overcome debt repayment problems, unlike short-term Stand-By Arrangements.

quiz.q: Why do developing countries argue that IMF loan conditionalities undermine their national sovereignty?
options: They require borrowing governments to transfer judicial authority over financial disputes to foreign international tribunals.
They compel borrowing countries to adopt domestic economic reforms favored by developed creditor nations.
They mandate that borrowing states replace their national currencies permanently with an international reserve asset.
They suspend borrowing nations from voting representation within the Board of Governors during stabilization programs.
quiz.why: Developing countries argue that conditionalities erode sovereignty because the IMF compels borrowers to adopt economic reforms favored by developed countries.

quiz.q: Under the stalled 2010 IMF governance reforms, how would representation on the Board of Executive Directors change?
options: The total number of executive directors would expand from twenty-four to thirty-two member seats.
Developing countries would receive permanently reserved executive director seats equal to the G7 economies.
All executive directors would be elected, ending the privilege of individual countries appointing their own.
Executive director positions would rotate annually among all member nations in strict alphabetical sequence.
quiz.why: The 2010 reforms agreed that no country would maintain the privilege of appointing its own executive director, making all directors elected.

quiz.q: Why does the United States possess an effective unilateral veto over substantive decisions in the IMF?
options: The IMF charter explicitly grants an exclusive statutory veto to the single largest financial contributor.
The United States finances more than half of all emergency bailout funds deployed during global crises.
Substantive policy resolutions require unanimous formal approval from every finance minister on the Board of Governors.
Major decisions require an eighty-five percent supermajority, while the United States holds around seventeen percent of votes.
quiz.why: Because substantive decisions require an 85% supermajority and the United States holds approximately 17% of total votes, nothing can pass without American consent.
